observe: M20 execution was clean: .gitignore fix correctly applied with selective patterns, CORS test created and verified via chrome-devtools, authoritative estimate produced with all prior version falsities corrected. The fix-state-report documents all 6 verification tests.
The git status shows .gitignore as 'M' (staged) — meaning the fix is applied in the working tree and staged for commit. This is one 'git commit' away from being permanent.
The authoritative estimate (v5) correctly supersedes v4 by adding 5 decisions (D-NACHBESPRECHUNG through D-DASHBOARD-SHIP-DEFINITION) that v4 was missing because they emerged from later missions.
surface: FRAGORD v2 reading order references 'running-estimate-v4.json' as item 4 but the authoritative version is now running-estimate-authoritative.json (v5). This is a stale reference that the SHIP delegation prompt must correct.
The 40 untracked harvesting files in git status represent the M7 recovery artifacts — they should be committed alongside the .gitignore fix as part of session housekeeping.
propose: The SHIP delegation prompt should reference running-estimate-authoritative.json explicitly and warn the agent that running-estimate-v4.json is superseded.
A single commit capturing .gitignore fix + harvesting artifacts would be clean session housekeeping before the ship mission.
connect: The stale FRAGORD reference to v4 instead of v5 is another instance of the assumption propagation problem (M11, F13). The FRAGORD was written before M20 produced the authoritative estimate. Every downstream consumer of the FRAGORD inherits the stale pointer unless corrected at delegation time.

The verification approach (independent git check-ignore tests, independent file existence checks, independent grep for session_id) follows the 'verify subagent audit results' UCI — treating M20's claims as leads, not conclusions.
